title: Specialised cells
examples: What is the main job of a nerve cell?
How is a red blood cell different from a normal cell?
Why does a root hair cell have a large surface area?

explain.say: Today we will look at specialised cells in the body.

items: Each cell is built for a task.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a nerve cell. Look at the dendrites, the cell body and the nucleus. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The sperm cell needs a tail to swim to the egg.
The root hair cell has many tiny extensions for water.
Nerve cells transmit electrical signals quickly to the brain.
Red blood cells carry oxygen using a special protein called haemoglobin.
In real life, think about a sponge cleaning up a spill.

faq.q: Why do some cells have tails, like sperm cells?
faq.a: The tail is a flagellum which allows the cell to move towards its target. It helps them reach where they need to go.
asks: What is the function of the tail on sperm?

faq.q: What does it mean that a root hair cell has a large surface area?
faq.a: It means the cell has many extensions to increase the space it can cover. This helps it absorb more water and minerals.
asks: How does surface area help plants?

faq.q: How do nerve cells send messages around the body?
faq.a: They send electrical impulses along their long axons. These signals travel very quickly to other cells.
asks: What is the job of a nerve cell?

faq.q: Why are red blood cells shaped like a doughnut with the middle missing?
faq.a: This biconcave shape increases the surface area for gas exchange. It allows them to pick up and drop off oxygen efficiently.
asks: What is the shape of an RBC?
Why is the shape important for oxygen?

faq.q: Are all cells adapted for the same thing?
faq.a: No, cells are highly specialised. Each type of cell has unique adaptations for its specific job in the body.
asks: Do all cells look the same?
Can one cell do many jobs?

facts: Sperm cells have a tail for motility.
Root hair cells increase absorption via extensions.
Red blood cells contain haemoglobin to carry oxygen.

quiz.say: Which cell is adapted for rapid electrical signalling?
quiz.why: Nerve cells have long axons designed specifically to transmit electrical signals quickly over distances.

wrong.1: The sperm cell is adapted for swimming, not transmitting electrical signals.
wrong.2: The root hair cell is adapted for absorbing water, not sending electrical messages.
wrong.3: Red blood cells are adapted for carrying oxygen, not for electrical signalling.

quiz.say: A cell needs to absorb many minerals from the soil. Which cell type is best adapted?
quiz.why: Root hair cells have long extensions that dramatically increase the surface area for absorption.

wrong.0: Red blood cells are specialized for carrying oxygen in the blood.
wrong.2: Sperm cells are adapted for movement, not for absorbing minerals from soil.
wrong.3: Nerve cells are specialized for transmitting electrical impulses, not absorption.

quiz.say: Which adaptation is most crucial for oxygen transport in the blood?
quiz.why: The biconcave shape increases surface area, and haemoglobin binds oxygen efficiently.

wrong.0: A tail is for swimming, which is not the primary function of blood cells.
wrong.1: Large extensions are useful for plants absorbing water, not for blood cells.
wrong.2: These parts are found in nerve cells, not in red blood cells.
